items.title: The snake lemma in an abelian category
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the snake lemma for a commutative diagram with exact rows in an abelian category, giving both the connecting map with its defining universal property and the exactness of the resulting six-term sequence with the two extra injectivity and surjectivity statements (statement lines 1228-1265). The proof is a complete argument: uniqueness and the construction of the connecting map are read off from the displayed diagram (proof lines 1268-1327), the vanishing of one composite is computed (proof lines 1329-1335), and exactness at the middle term is obtained by two applications of the fibre-product criterion which produce the auxiliary objects and morphism (proof lines 1337-1339), after which the conclusion follows from a named kernel-sequence lemma and duality (proof lines 1340-1342). The non-formal content is the construction of delta through the two cartesian squares and the exactness test. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
